title: Aligot (Stretchy Cheese and Garlic Mash)
summary: Potato mashed with garlic, cream and plenty of melting cheese is beaten hard until it turns glossy and stretches into long ribbons. It's rich, garlicky mash taken to its most indulgent extreme.
equipment: sturdy silicone spatula or wooden spoon

ingredients.item: floury or all-purpose potatoes (such as russet or Yukon Gold)
fine salt, for the cooking water
young tomme fraîche, or a mix of alpine-style cheese and mozzarella (microbial rennet), grated
ingredients.note: the mozzarella gives the stretch if you cannot find tomme

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Cover the peeled potato chunks with cold water, add the salt, whole garlic clove and thyme sprigs, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until very tender. Cooking the garlic and thyme in the water infuses the potato gently without any harsh raw garlic flavour.

steps.title: Drain and rice
steps.text: Drain well, discard the garlic and thyme, and pass the potatoes through a ricer straight back into the dry pan. Ricing while still hot keeps the purée smooth with no lumps to fight later.

steps.title: Beat in butter and garlic
steps.text: Over low heat, beat in the butter and the grated raw garlic until fully melted and smooth.

steps.title: Add the cream
steps.text: Beat in the hot cream in two additions, working each one in fully before adding the next, until the mixture is smooth and glossy.

steps.title: Melt in the cheese
steps.text: Add the cheese a handful at a time, beating hard in a figure-of-eight motion and lifting the spatula after each addition, until the mash turns glossy and stretches in long ribbons, about 4-6 minutes. This constant beating develops the cheese's elasticity — too much heat at this stage would make it split and turn oily, so keep it low.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Taste and season with the extra salt, then serve immediately while it's at its stretchiest, as aligot firms up quickly as it cools.

tips: Keep the heat low once the cheese goes in — too much heat makes the mixture split and turn oily instead of staying smooth and elastic.
Beat hard and consistently; a half-hearted stir is the most common reason aligot doesn't stretch properly.
If you can't find tomme fraîche, a mix of alpine-style cheese (microbial rennet) and mozzarella gives a similar pull.
Serve it the moment it's ready — aligot firms up and loses its stretch as it cools.
storage: Aligot is really at its best eaten fresh, but leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently over low heat, beating in a splash of warm cream or milk, until piping hot and stretchy again. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
